headline: S&P 500 fell a fifth day Wednesday (-0.2%, below its 200-day average); Dow -1.1%, Nasdaq +0.4%. Fed minutes say nearly all officials see more rate hikes ahead. Health insurers sank on a Medicare audit rule; oil, gold and miners fell. Anthropic IPO priced at $83, trades today; Walmart reports today.

sectors.why: No clear sector news. Hawkish Fed minutes and a 10-year yield near 5.1% stay a mild headwind.
No clear US telecom news. Yields above 5% compete with telecom dividends.
Pending home sales fell 4.7% in October to the lowest since at least 2001, and Fed minutes point to more rate hikes, which weighs on homes, cars and furniture.
No clear sector news. A stronger dollar and higher rates are mixed for staples; Walmart's results today set the consumer tone.
No clear sector news. Strong retail results suggest spending is holding up, but rate hikes lie ahead.
No clear sector news. Health distributors may feel some pressure from the new Medicare audit rule, but the hit is on insurers.
Nvidia beat and guided about $130B next quarter but fell 2.9% for a fifth straight loss amid CEO turmoil; AMD and Broadcom rose. AI demand is strong, but leadership questions cloud the leader.
Oil fell about 3% to near $83 WTI on rising US crude and fuel stockpiles and energy was the weakest sector, though Middle East supply risk can reverse this quickly.
Higher rates help lending margins, but crypto-linked stocks fell and the dollar's jump to a 19-month high adds uncertainty.
A CMS proposed rule widens Medicare Advantage audits to recover about $90B from 2027 to 2036. UnitedHealth fell 10%, Humana 13%, Elevance and Centene about 7%.
No clear sector news for drug and device makers; the Medicare rule targets insurers.
No clear sector news. Higher rates are a mild headwind for project financing.
No clear news for this mixed group.
Gold fell about 3.5% and copper sank as the dollar hit a 19-month high on hawkish Fed minutes; Freeport fell about 7% and Newmont about 6%.
No clear sector news. A strong dollar is a mild headwind for chemical exporters.
No clear sector news. Rate hikes ahead are a mild headwind for capital spending.
Target, TJX and Lowe's beat and raised outlooks (helped by tariff refunds); TJX rose 8%, Target 4%, Amazon 3.8% on the Anthropic IPO. Walmart reports today, so this can change.
Palo Alto jumped about 10% on strong results and a raised outlook, and Anthropic's IPO priced above range, but software was hit by AI-replacement fears this week.
Lower oil helps fuel costs, but there is no clear sector news.
No clear sector news. Yields near 5.1% and likely Fed hikes compete with utility dividends.

avoid.HUM: CMS proposed wider Medicare Advantage audits recovering payments; shares fell 13% and the rule's comment period keeps the risk open.
avoid.UNH: Same CMS Medicare Advantage audit proposal hit UnitedHealth 10%; the final rule outcome is still unknown.
